newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 9.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--As the government and protesting farmers maintained their positions for the 12th day, Greece looks forward to a 10-day fiesta of strikes and protests from teachers, pensioners, doctors and others.

--A new poll shows failed leadership contender George Souflias to be the favourite of conservative opposition New Democracy supporters in what will be a rerun of the leadership challenge at the party's congress.
--At least 15 brokerage firms are involved in the Delta affair which rocked the Athens bourse recently, a young businessman says.
--The economy does not have the margins to satisfy 'groundless and dangerous demands', Greece's European Commissioner Christos Papoutsis says.
--The government moves to put a lid on overtime and other payments in the public sector.
--Veteran leftist Leonidis Kyrkos calls for immediate dialogue between Athens and Ankara: Athens should not extend its territorial waters to 12 miles in return for concessions from Ankara, he adds.
--The government will impose upper limits on prices on meat and fresh food in its first intervention in the market following the first appearances of cases of profiteering.

--The president of the republic gave a lesson in democracy over the weekend to Prime Minister Costas Simitis, visiting flooded Xanthi by road, stopping to talk to protesting farmers at their roadblocks on the way.
